entries.definition: physically or spiritually homeless or deprived of security
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames the condition as something stripped away, whether the security lost is literal shelter or inward footing, where *homeless* only reports the absence.
examples: made a living out of shepherding dispossessed people from one country to another

entries.definition: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Treats the ruin as finished business, the consequences ending things rather than merely wrecking them as *disastrous* allows.
examples: such doctrines, if true, would be absolutely fatal to my theory
it is fatal to enter any war without the will to win it

entries.definition: (of events) having extremely unfortunate or dire consequences; bringing ruin
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Weights the ruin with inevitability, as though the outcome were settled before the event, a solemnity *disastrous* never claims.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Almost fond pity for someone luck keeps failing, entirely free of the contempt in *pathetic*.

entries.definition: physically or spiritually homeless or deprived of security
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The flat naming term, covering the person without a roof and the one without spiritual anchorage alike, and carrying none of the grievance in *dispossessed*.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Wretchedness thick enough to be uncomfortable to look at, far heavier than the light sympathy of *hapless*.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest of these, granting that the pity is deserved and stopping there, where *pathetic* adds scorn to it.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Pity curdled into contempt, looking down at what it pities in a way *piteous* never does.
examples: the shabby room struck her as extraordinarily pathetic

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Elevated and unmixed, the suffering moving whoever sees it rather than lowering the sufferer as *pathetic* does.

entries.definition: deserving or inciting pity
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Sits on the hinge, able to ask for pity or to grant it while withholding respect, where *piteous* only asks.

entries.definition: physically or spiritually homeless or deprived of security
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Keeps a bleak physical picture even when the exposure it names is inward, which makes it starker than *homeless*.

entries.definition: not favored by fortune; marked or accompanied by or resulting in ill fortune
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The mildest way to mark ill luck, registering that fortune went against someone with none of the ruin *calamitous* insists on.
examples: an unfortunate night for all concerned

entries.definition: (of eggs) no longer edible
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A flat verdict on an egg: not merely aging but past eating, and far blunter about it than *stale*.

entries.definition: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The blankest possible condemnation — no mold, no smell, no rot named, just the ruling that the food can no longer be eaten or used.

entries.definition: having lost freshness through passage of time
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Understated to the edge of euphemism: it says only that time has passed and the freshness with it, leaving the eater to reach the conclusion *stale* states outright.
examples: dogs attempting to catch a cold scent

entries.definition: touched by rot or decay
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Formal, almost delicate for what it names: rot or decay has only touched the thing, not finished it as in *rotten*.

entries.definition: not fresh today
entries.label: neutral
entries.tone: Purely a matter of the calendar — it dates the food and leaves the verdict unspoken, where *stale* delivers one.
examples: day-old bread is cheaper than fresh

entries.definition: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Disgust made literal: the ruin is not merely named but shown, with the flies' eggs and larvae sitting on it.

entries.definition: dried out
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Reports a texture rather than a decay — the food has dried out, not gone foul — which makes it the least damning word in the family.
examples: hard dry rolls left over from the day before

entries.definition: spoiled and covered with eggs and larvae of flies
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Carries the same infestation as *flyblown*, eggs and larvae alike, but puts the crawling larvae in front of you, which makes it the harder of the two to hear.

entries.definition: covered with or smelling of mold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: A specific and repellent charge — the growth seen on the food or smelled off it — where *bad* offers only a ruling.

entries.definition: covered with or smelling of mold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling of *moldy*, just as exact about mold either seen or smelled.

entries.definition: covered with or smelling of mold
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The gentlest of the three words for this condition, charging the same mold on the food or smell of mold off it with none of *moldy*'s bluntness.

entries.definition: (used of decomposing oils or fats) having a rank smell or taste usually due to a chemical change or decomposition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Fixes on fats and oils gone over and on the rank smell or taste that gives them away, a sensory accusation rather than *bad*'s bare ruling.

entries.definition: having decayed or disintegrated; usually implies foulness
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The word for full collapse — decay carried through to disintegration, and foulness with it.
examples: dead and rotten in his grave

entries.definition: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Frames the same loss — no longer edible or usable — as damage done to the food, a ruin rather than *bad*'s bare verdict.

entries.definition: (of foodstuffs) not in an edible or usable condition
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: British spelling of *spoiled*, identical in force and equally final about food past eating or using.
examples: a refrigerator full of spoilt food

entries.definition: lacking freshness, palatability, or showing deterioration from age
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word here for the whole slide out of freshness — taste gone, condition gone with age — without yet ruling the food inedible the way *bad* does.

entries.definition: splendid
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise at its plainest - splendid, with none of the awe *sublime* carries or the record standing behind *storied*.
examples: the bright stars of stage and screen

entries.definition: having an illustrious past
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The illustrious past registered as acclaim - others have noticed, which *historied* does not bother to say.

entries.definition: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Excellence pushed past the human scale until it reads as god-given rather than merely achieved.

entries.definition: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The most rarefied way to say that same god-touched excellence - ornate where *divine* is direct.

entries.definition: inspiring awe
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Awe pitched at its loftiest and most ornate, where *sublime* delivers the same awe in a word that can be said plainly.
examples: well-meaning ineptitude that rises to empyreal absurdity

entries.definition: inspiring awe
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Matched to *empyreal* in force - awe as sheer altitude, something the eye has to be raised to.

entries.definition: having or deserving or conferring glory
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The family's full measure - glory had, glory deserved and glory handed on, where *illustrious* claims only the having and the conferring.

entries.definition: having an illustrious past
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The same illustrious past stated as plain fact rather than applause, and more formal for it than *celebrated*.

entries.definition: having or conferring glory
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Glory as both possession and gift - it holds glory and lends it out, without *glorious*'s further claim that the glory is deserved.

entries.definition: characterized by ardent emotion or intensity or brilliance
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Praise for a white heat, whether of ardent feeling, of intensity or of sheer brilliance - it burns where *lustrous* only shines.

entries.definition: being of such surpassing excellence as to suggest inspiration by the gods
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The mildest of the three - it credits the surpassing excellence to something breathed in from outside without naming the gods as *divine* and *elysian* do.

entries.definition: brilliant
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Brilliance as a finish on the surface - it gleams, where *incandescent* burns from inside.
examples: set a lustrous example for others to follow

entries.definition: having an illustrious past
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: The illustrious past turned into something worth recounting - it implies a tale, where *celebrated* implies only admirers.

entries.definition: inspiring awe
entries.label: positive
entries.tone: Awe that arrests rather than merely pleases - the word here that admits to being overwhelmed.
examples: the sublime beauty of the night

entries.definition: shockingly brutal or cruel
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The shock sits inside the word, so the brutality is reported as something that appals rather than as something merely wrong.

entries.definition: characterized by wickedness or immorality
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: The plainest word in the set made to carry wickedness, and the flatness is its force — *monstrous* shouts where this one only states.

entries.definition: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Absolute and unshaded: the wickedness is treated as total rather than as a streak, and no mitigation is offered.
examples: his black heart has concocted yet another black deed

entries.definition: tending to corrupt or pervert
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Clinical in shape: it names an ongoing capacity to spoil rather than passing sentence on a single act.

entries.definition: stemming from evil characteristics or forces; wicked or dishonorable
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Suggestive rather than accusing, placing the evil behind what is visible — in what a thing comes out of as much as in the thing itself.
examples: Darth Vader of the dark side

entries.definition: extremely evil or cruel; expressive of cruelty or befitting hell
entries.label: negative
entries.tone: Attributes the cruelty to a nature rather than a choice, as though it were the whole of what the thing is.
examples: something demonic in him — something that could be cruel
